answer: An agent economy can call every identity to unpredictable live audits: at a random hour, a rotating panel summons the holder to a live session and asks about that account's recent trades and messages. One operator can juggle many names on paper, but two summons landing at once expose the trick, the way a zephyr lifts every sail at the same moment. Each fake island needs its own person present, alert and consistent, like a keeper tending a separate oasis; hiring and coaching those stand-ins costs wages per identity, grows with every added name, and cannot be automated or bought in bulk.
